# Spec: run-survival
<!-- Generated by /hefesto:hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-09 -->
<!-- Board item: HEF-25 — runs survive the orchestrator's death and never starve the host: own scopes, memory-aware concurrency -->
<!-- req-coverage: scoped -->

## Overview

On a 24 GB host, `systemd-oomd` killed Claude Code's transient scope twice in one minute. The user slice had sat
above the 60 % memory-pressure limit for 20 s, and one scope held 10.6 GB: the orchestrator, three
`claude -p` workers, their reviewer subagents, a `shellcheck` over a 5000+-line file, and the smoke suite. Every
worker died with the orchestrator. `hooks/session-launch.sh` runs as a child of the orchestrator's Bash tool, and the
worker `claude -p` is the launcher's child (`:684`), so both sit in the orchestrator's scope and process group.
This feature makes a launch survive and keeps it from starving the host:
- each run is detached into its own unit;
- the number of concurrent runs is capped;
- a launch is refused when memory is short or under pressure;
- `shellcheck` runs only on changed shell files, under a memory limit, and skips very large files;
- `hefesto-setup.sh --check` reports an `systemd-oomd` set to its default user-slice limit.

## Decisions (made here, from the code — no clarification needed)

- **D1 — what is detached is the launcher's run tail, not only `claude`.** The launcher waits on the worker
  (`:691`), reads its result back, and writes the ledger (`transcribe`). It also renews the lease that tells a live
  claim from a dead one (`:688`, `ledger-lanes.sh lease_stale`). A worker that survived without its launcher would
  finish unrecorded, and after 5 min it would be reaped while still running. So in run mode, after every check and
  just before the claim, `session-launch.sh` re-executes itself detached with the same arguments. The detached copy
  claims with `--pid` set to its own pid, starts the worker, renews the lease, and transcribes. The caller waits for
  it and passes its exit code and output on. While the orchestrator lives, the exit-notice flow in
  `commands/hef.orchestrate.md` step 3 is unchanged.
- **D2 — how it detaches.**
  - When `systemd-run` is on PATH and the user manager answers, the run starts as
    `systemd-run --user --scope --collect --quiet --unit hefesto-<id>-<role>-<tag> -- setsid …`. The scope moves it
    out of the orchestrator's cgroup, which is what oomd kills. `setsid` moves it out of the process group and session
    that a closed terminal or a stopped Bash tool signals.
  - Otherwise, when `setsid` is on PATH, it uses `setsid` alone.
  - Otherwise (stock macOS has neither), the launch runs attached as today, with one stderr line:
    `session-launch: no systemd-run or setsid — the run is attached to this shell`.
  - `--dry-run`, `--prepare` and `--finish` never detach. They start no session.
- **D3 — the detached copy never writes to the caller's pipes.** Its stdout and stderr go to
  `<RUNDIR>/<id>.<tag>.launcher.out` and `.launcher.err` (together, "the launcher log"). They sit beside the run's
  event stream in `~/.cache/hefesto/runs`, where no sandbox writes. While the caller is alive, it copies that log to its own stdout and stderr after the detached copy
  exits, then exits with the copy's code. A dead caller therefore cannot take the run down with SIGPIPE.
- **D4 — stopping a run stays deliberate and goes through the run's own pid.** The caller forwards no signal: an oomd
  SIGKILL cannot be trapped anyway, and the item says a session kill must not take the workers. The detached launcher
  keeps today's TERM/INT/HUP trap (`:690`): it stops its worker and records exit 143. So
  `kill <owner.pid from ledger.sh show <id>>` stops a run, and the docs say so. The sentence in
  `hef.orchestrate.md` that says "a launcher that is stopped stops its worker first" is rewritten to match.
- **D5 — `orchestrate.max_concurrent_runs` is enforced in `ledger.sh claim`, under its lock**, the same place as the
  stage limits (`ledger.sh:457–469`). It counts live owners with a `pid`, meaning launched runs, across the whole
  ledger: all repos and all roles, verify included. A `--mode interactive` claim is a lane, not a run, and is neither
  counted nor refused. Verify is not exempt here: the orchestrator's step 3 already relaunches a `verify`-phase entry
  with no owner, so a refused verifier is not stranded: it is picked up once its last run is more than 10 minutes old
  (the window in `hef.orchestrate.md` step 3), and the docs say so. Valid values are a whole
  number from 1 to 8, default 2, validated like `max_builders`. The refusal says
  `busy: <n> runs at once (orchestrate.max_concurrent_runs <lim>): <id> (owned by …), …`.
- **D6 — the memory gate runs in `session-launch.sh`, in run mode only, before the claim, in the copy that
  claims** (the detached copy, or the attached launcher when no detacher exists). The measurement is taken at the
  moment that matters, and the detach marker grants no way around it (plan review 2026-11-09).
  - It reads `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo` and `some avg60` from `/proc/pressure/memory`. It refuses when
    available MiB < `orchestrate.min_free_mb` (whole number ≥ 0, default 4096; 0 turns the floor off) or when
    avg60 > 50. The refusal says `busy: memory — <MemAvailable> MiB available < <min> MiB` or
    `busy: memory pressure some avg60=<v> > 50`, and it claims and records nothing.
  - A missing `/proc/meminfo` (macOS) skips the gate, and a missing PSI file skips the pressure half, each with one
    stderr note. The launch is not refused.
  - The 50 % pressure threshold is fixed, as the item states it.
- **D7 — busy refusals have their own exit code, 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL).** That goes for both the memory gate and the
  run cap. `session-launch.sh` maps a claim refusal whose message starts `busy:` to 75. Every other refusal keeps
  exit 1. `hef.orchestrate.md` step 3 treats exit 75 as "skip this stage, retry next pass", reported in one line and
  not as a failure. The stage-limit refusal that already exists keeps exit 1 and its wording (no change asked).
- **D8 — the `/proc` test seam.** `HEFESTO_PROC_MEMINFO` and `HEFESTO_PROC_PRESSURE` override the two paths only
  when `HEFESTO_TRUSTED_TOP` is unset, which covers a terminal and the smoke suite (`LANE_MODE=0`, `:110`). In lane
  mode the real `/proc` files are always read, so a lane cannot point the gate at a fake file.
- **D9 — shellcheck: one helper, called from every place that runs it.**
  - A new subcommand, `speckit-helper.sh shellcheck-changed [--base <ref>] [--severity <s>]`, finds the changed
    `.sh`/`.bash` files: the diff against the merge base with the PR base (the existing `pr_base`), plus staged and
    unstaged changes.
  - It skips any file over 3000 lines with one line:
    `shellcheck: skipped <f> (<n> lines > 3000) — too large to check here; split it, or check it by hand`.
    (Measured at the round-3 plan review: `tests/smoke.sh`, 6818 lines, runs out of memory under `ulimit -v` at 2, 4
    and 8 GiB, so no bounded run checks it. Splitting `tests/smoke.sh` into sourced parts under 3000 lines is a
    follow-up item.)
  - It runs each remaining file as `shellcheck -S <s>` in a subshell under `ulimit -v`. The limit is owned by
    `hooks/host-limits.sh` (`HL_SC_VMEM_KB`, 2 GiB unless the first implementation task's measurement raises it).
    Exit 1 is a finding. Any other non-zero exit is "could not check", the same split as
    `quality-before-commit.sh:133–139`.
  - Exit codes: 0 = every changed file checked and clean (or no changed shell files); 1 = a finding; 2 = incomplete
    (a file skipped or not checked, or shellcheck not installed), never read as clean (constitution 5). Every skipped
    or unchecked file is listed.
  - A sibling subcommand, `speckit-helper.sh shellcheck-files [--severity <s>] <file…>`, runs the same bounded runner
    over named files with no line skip; `commands/hef.doctor.md` uses it in place of its `hooks/*.sh` glob.
  - The smoke suite's tier-2 guard runs one file per process through the same bounded runner, with the same
    3000-line skip, and its list gains `tests/*.sh`. An oversize file prints one visible `skip` line (the shape of the
    guard's existing "not installed" skip) naming the file and the follow-up, and the guard stays green. A "could not
    check" on a file under the limit fails the suite.
  - `commands/hef.quality.md` and `commands/hef.verify.md` tell the session to check shell files only through this
    helper, never `shellcheck` over a tree or a glob.
  - `hooks/quality-before-commit.sh` applies the same 3000-line skip and `ulimit -v` to its staged-file loop.
- **D10 — the oomd report is advice, and it never offers to disable oomd.** The item text lists
  `systemctl disable --now systemd-oomd` as a choice. That was measured as the wrong one on the same host on
  2026-11-09: with oomd off, the machine thrashed into a hard freeze within the hour. `--check` therefore prints a
  `setup: note:` line, which does not change its exit code or `setup: ok`, when all of these hold:
  - `systemctl is-active systemd-oomd` reads `active`;
  - `systemctl show user@<uid>.service -p ManagedOOMMemoryPressure -p ManagedOOMMemoryPressureLimit` reads
    `kill`, with the limit unset (`0`, `0%`, or empty, which means oomd's 60 % default) or exactly `60%`.

  The note then prints:
  - the system drop-in text for `/etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/90-hefesto-oomd.conf`
    (`[Service]` / `ManagedOOMMemoryPressureLimit=80%`), and `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`, with "your choice — the
    script writes nothing";
  - a line saying oomd should stay on, because the hefesto run cap and memory gate are what size the load.

  The plan review (2026-11-09) reviewed this and kept it, and the item's owner confirmed it (Clarifications): the
  item's disable option is withdrawn.
- **D11 — no setting is written by setup for the new keys.** `max_concurrent_runs` and `min_free_mb` live in
  `.claude/project-status.json` (`orchestrate`), like `max_builders`, and their defaults apply when they are absent.

## User Scenarios

### US1: A run survives the orchestrator's scope being killed [P1]
- **Given** a host with `systemd-run` (or only `setsid`) and an item in phase `tasks`
- **When** the orchestrator launches `session-launch.sh implement <id>`, and the orchestrator's process tree is then
  killed with SIGKILL
- **Then**:
  - the launcher's run tail and its `claude -p` worker keep running in their own scope or session;
  - the lease keeps being renewed;
  - when the worker ends, the ledger records the run and the transcription (phase `verify`, or a block);
  - the next orchestrator pass sees the outcome from the ledger alone.
- **Edge**: with neither `systemd-run` nor `setsid` → the launch runs attached as today, with one stderr line saying
  so, and an otherwise unchanged ledger outcome.
- **Edge**: `systemd-run` is on PATH but the user manager is unreachable → falls back to `setsid`.
- **Error/negative**: `--dry-run`, `--prepare` and `--finish` never call `systemd-run` or `setsid`. A detached run
  never writes to the caller's stdout or stderr after the caller is gone: no SIGPIPE, and the run is still
  transcribed.

### US2: The orchestrator, while alive, sees the run exactly as before [P1]
- **Given** a detached launch from a background Bash call
- **When** the run ends
- **Then** the caller exits with the run's exit code and prints the run's stdout (the final ledger entry) and stderr,
  so the exit-notice flow in `hef.orchestrate.md` step 3 is unchanged
- **Edge**: a refusal inside the detached copy (a claim refusal, for example) → the caller exits with its code and
  shows its message
- **Error/negative**: killing the caller (TERM) does NOT stop the run. `kill <owner.pid>` does: the run's own trap
  stops the worker and records exit 143.

### US3: At most `max_concurrent_runs` launched runs at once [P1]
- **Given** `orchestrate.max_concurrent_runs` absent (default 2) and two entries each claimed with a live `--pid`
- **When** a third launch claims, in any role or repo of the ledger
- **Then** the claim is refused with `busy: 2 runs at once (orchestrate.max_concurrent_runs 2): …`, and the launch
  exits 75 with nothing recorded on the third entry
- **Edge**: interactive (lane) claims are not counted, so two runs plus one interactive claim still let a lane prepare
- **Edge**: `max_concurrent_runs: 3` → the third launch passes and the fourth is refused
- **Error/negative**: `max_concurrent_runs: 0`, `9`, `"two"` or `1.5` → `ledger claim` dies naming the value and the
  expected range 1–8

### US4: A launch is refused when the host is short of memory [P1]
- **Given** a `meminfo` fixture with `MemAvailable: 2097152 kB` (2048 MiB) and `min_free_mb` absent (4096)
- **When** `session-launch.sh plan <id>` runs
- **Then** it exits 75 with `busy: memory — 2048 MiB available < 4096 MiB`, and neither claims nor writes anything
  in the ledger
- **Edge**: a PSI fixture with `some avg10=0.00 avg60=63.20 …` and plenty of memory → exit 75,
  `busy: memory pressure some avg60=63.20 > 50`
- **Edge**: `min_free_mb: 0` with low memory → not refused for memory; pressure is still checked
- **Edge**: no meminfo or no PSI file → that check is skipped with one stderr note, and the launch proceeds
- **Error/negative**: `min_free_mb: -1` or `"4G"` → exit 1 naming the value and the shape (a whole number of MiB ≥ 0).
  `--dry-run`/`--prepare` are never refused for memory.

### US5: shellcheck never runs the host out of memory [P2]
- **Given** a branch that changed `hooks/a.sh` (40 lines) and `tests/big.sh` (3500 lines)
- **When** `/hefesto:hef.quality` or `/hefesto:hef.verify` checks shell files through
  `speckit-helper.sh shellcheck-changed`
- **Then**:
  - only `hooks/a.sh` is checked, under `ulimit -v`;
  - `tests/big.sh` gets the one-line skipped note;
  - a finding in `a.sh` exits 1;
  - a shellcheck killed or out of memory is reported as "could not check" and exits 2.
- **Edge**: no shell file changed → `shellcheck: no changed shell files`, exit 0
- **Edge**: `quality-before-commit.sh` with a staged 3500-line `.sh` → skipped with the note (an advisory) and not
  checked; a 40-line one is still checked, and a finding still blocks
- **Error/negative**: shellcheck not installed → `shellcheck: not installed — skipped`, exit 2 (incomplete; the
  commit hook keeps its advisory, never blocking)

### US6: Setup check reports a default oomd user-slice limit [P2]
- **Given** a fake `systemctl` reporting oomd `active`, and `user@<uid>.service` with
  `ManagedOOMMemoryPressure=kill` and an unset or `60%` limit
- **When** `hefesto-setup.sh --check` runs
- **Then** it prints a `setup: note:` naming the 60 % default, the drop-in text with its path, and the
  `daemon-reload` command, says oomd should stay on, and keeps the same exit code and `setup: ok` as without the note
- **Edge**: limit `80%`, oomd inactive, or no `systemctl` (macOS) → no note
- **Error/negative**: the output never contains `systemctl disable`, and `--check` writes nothing

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | In run mode (not `--dry-run`, `--prepare` or `--finish`), `session-launch.sh` re-executes its run tail (claim → worker → lease → transcribe) detached: `systemd-run --user --scope … -- setsid …` when `systemd-run` is usable, otherwise `setsid`, otherwise attached with one stderr note (D1, D2) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | The detached copy writes stdout/stderr only to `<RUNDIR>/<id>.<tag>.launcher.out` / `.launcher.err`, and the claim's `--pid` is the detached copy's own pid (D1, D3) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | The caller waits for the detached copy, then prints its log (stdout and stderr) and exits with its exit code. It forwards no signal; the detached launcher keeps its TERM/INT/HUP trap (D3, D4) | P1 | US2 |
| FR-004 | `ledger.sh claim` with `--pid` refuses with a message starting `busy:` when the live owners holding a `pid` in the ledger already reach `orchestrate.max_concurrent_runs` (1–8, default 2). Interactive claims are neither counted nor refused (D5) | P1 | US3 |
| FR-005 | An invalid `max_concurrent_runs` makes `ledger claim` die, naming the value and the range 1–8 | P1 | US3 |
| FR-006 | Before the claim, in run mode, `session-launch.sh` refuses with exit 75 when `MemAvailable` (MiB) < `orchestrate.min_free_mb` (default 4096; 0 = off) or PSI `some avg60` > 50. Each message carries the measured value and the limit, and nothing is claimed or recorded (D6) | P1 | US4 |
| FR-007 | A missing meminfo or PSI file skips that check with one stderr note. An invalid `min_free_mb` exits 1 with the value and the expected shape. The `/proc` paths can be overridden only when `HEFESTO_TRUSTED_TOP` is unset (D6, D8) | P1 | US4 |
| FR-008 | A claim refused as `busy:` makes `session-launch.sh` exit 75; all other refusals keep their codes (D7) | P1 | US3 |
| FR-009 | `speckit-helper.sh shellcheck-changed` checks only the changed `.sh`/`.bash` files, each under `ulimit -v <HL_SC_VMEM_KB>` (default in `host-limits.sh`). Files over 3000 lines are skipped with the one-line note. Exit 0 = all checked and clean, 1 = a finding, 2 = incomplete (skipped, not checked, or not installed), each such file listed (D9) | P2 | US5 |
| FR-010 | `quality-before-commit.sh` applies the same 3000-line skip (as an advisory) and `ulimit -v` to its staged shell files (D9) | P2 | US5 |
| FR-011 | `commands/hef.quality.md` and `commands/hef.verify.md` route every shell-file check through `shellcheck-changed` and say never to shellcheck a tree or glob (D9) | P2 | US5 |
| FR-014 | `speckit-helper.sh shellcheck-files` runs the bounded runner over named files (no line skip); `commands/hef.doctor.md` uses it instead of a glob; the tier-2 guard in `tests/smoke.sh` checks one file per process through the same runner with the 3000-line skip (a visible `skip` line per oversize file), also covers `tests/*.sh`, and fails on "could not check" for a file under the limit (D9) | P2 | US5 |
| FR-012 | `hefesto-setup.sh --check` prints a `setup: note:` with the drop-in and `daemon-reload` when oomd is active with a default (unset or 60 %) user-slice limit. It never prints `systemctl disable`, writes nothing, and leaves the exit code unchanged (D10) | P2 | US6 |
| FR-013 | `commands/hef.orchestrate.md` step 3: exit 75 = busy, skip and retry next pass; a verifier refused with 75 is picked up by the "phase verify, no owner" rule only after its 10-minute window, and both step 3 and the quickstart say so. The stage-pass text (`hef.orchestrate.md:358`, "a launch that exits non-zero is reported with its stderr") reports exit 75 as "busy — next pass", never as a failure, and its `done` doorbell says so. A run survives the orchestrator and is picked up from the ledger, and `kill <owner.pid>` stops a run. Plus `docs/quickstart.md`/`.pt-BR.md` (config keys), `docs/hooks.md` (helper row), and a `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry (D4, D7) | P2 | US2, US3 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | Fake `systemd-run` and `setsid` on PATH record their argv. A launch with the fake `claude` records `--user --scope` then `setsid`; with only `setsid`, it records `setsid`; with neither, it prints the attached note; `--dry-run` records nothing | smoke, cites `run-survival/FR-001` |
| SC-002 | The caller's exit code and output equal the run's. After SIGKILL of the caller, the run still writes its transcription to the ledger | smoke (fake claude that sleeps, kill -9 the caller), cites FR-002, FR-003 |
| SC-003 | Two live `--pid` claims, then a third `claim` → `busy:` and rc≠0; the launch → exit 75; an interactive claim passes | smoke, cites FR-004, FR-008 |
| SC-004 | A meminfo fixture at 2048 MiB → exit 75 and the entry unchanged (`cmp`); PSI avg60 63.2 → exit 75; `min_free_mb: 0` → passes | smoke, cites FR-006, FR-007 |
| SC-005 | A changed 3500-line file → skipped note; a 40-line file with an error → exit 1; a fake shellcheck exiting 137 → "could not check", exit 2; a fake shellcheck logs `ulimit -v` and the log shows `HL_SC_VMEM_KB`; the tier-2 guard invokes one process per file and prints a `skip` line for an oversize file. Structural greps: `hef.quality.md` and `hef.verify.md` name `shellcheck-changed`, and `hef.doctor.md` no longer runs shellcheck over `hooks/*.sh` | smoke, cites FR-009, FR-010, FR-011, FR-014 |
| SC-006 | A fake `systemctl` (active, kill, limit 0) → note with the drop-in, no `systemctl disable`, rc and `setup: ok` unchanged; limit `80%` → no note | smoke, cites FR-012 |
| SC-007 | Mutations, each caught by its check: (a) drop the detach call; (b) count interactive claims, or drop the cap check; (c) invert the MemAvailable comparison; (d) remove the 3000-line skip; (e) drop the oomd note's limit test; (f) drop the `busy:` → 75 mapping; (g) remove the `ulimit -v` line; (h) move the memory gate back to the caller only (a fixture-low launch through a fake `setsid` must still exit 75); (i) drop the `.started` condition from the retry (a copy that ran and refused must not be launched again); (j) drop the `LANE_MODE` test on the `/proc` seam (a lane-mode launch must not show the fixture value); (k) drop the `.started` path guard (a lane-mode launch with `HEFESTO_RUN_DETACHED` outside the runs folder must leave no `.started` file); (l) drop the `LANE_MODE` test on the `HEFESTO_RUN_DETACH=0` seam (a lane-mode launch with it set and both fake detachers on PATH must still record a detacher in the argv log) | smoke mutation lines (sed on copies) |
| SC-009 | Structural greps: `hef.orchestrate.md` names exit `75` (step 3 and the stage-pass text), the verifier's 10-minute wait, and `kill <owner.pid>`; `docs/quickstart.md` and `.pt-BR.md` name `max_concurrent_runs` and `min_free_mb` | smoke, cites FR-013 |
| SC-008 | `shellcheck -S warning` on every changed hook is clean; no hook newly goes over 500 code lines | tier-2 guard + `quality-before-commit.sh` delta gate |

## Out of Scope

- A per-run `MemoryMax=` on the scope (sizing each worker): the item does not ask for it (it asks for own scopes, a
  run cap and a memory gate), so it stays a follow-up item. Here the cap and the gate size the load. Confirmed at the
  plan review, 2026-11-09.
- Host-wide counting across several ledgers or projects: the cap is per ledger, and the memory gate is what covers
  the host.
- Re-attaching the orchestrator's Monitor or `run-follow.sh` to a run after the orchestrator restarts:
  `run-follow.sh <id>` already reads the run's files.
- Changing the stage limits or their exit code.

## Clarifications
Every other decision was made from the code and the item (see Decisions).

### Session 2026-11-09 (the item's owner)
- Q: D10 departs from the item, which offers `systemctl disable --now systemd-oomd`. Keep the departure? → A:
  Confirmed. `systemd-oomd` stays enabled on the host, and `--check` never suggests disabling it (disabling it on
  2026-11-09 froze the VM within the hour). The item's "or `systemctl disable --now systemd-oomd`" option is
  withdrawn.
- Q: The second plan review (REVISE_PLAN) asked for five changes. Apply them? → A: Apply all, and re-review until
  APPROVE (standing decision 2026-11-07, at most 5 rounds); stop for the person only on a product or design question:
  1. the detached copy restores only the `GIT_CONFIG_*` entries, never the whole `WORKER_ENV`;
  2. the `.started` marker is written before the pre-claim checks;
  3. the three missing mutations are added;
  4. the exit-75 verifier wait (the 10-minute "phase verify, no owner" window) is documented;
  5. the worker is started with `env -u HEFESTO_RUN_DETACHED`. (Round 3 kept the intent and changed the mechanism:
     the launcher runs `unset HEFESTO_RUN_DETACHED` right after the detach branch, so the worker never inherits it
     and the `--dry-run` line stays byte-identical to `tests/fixtures/launch-920.txt`.)
